citations.review_text: Admittedly I haven't played much, but without extensive modding (including upscaling) as soon as you enter the open world, the game runs [i]terribly[/i]. Low fps, major traversal stutters etc. I would avoid until a fix comes, if it ever does.

roughly 15-20 fps on high graphics
roughly 30-40 fps on medium graphics
roughly 40-50 fps on low graphics

but regardless of graphics settings, whenever im inside a place like a dungeon or a house I had 50-60 fps. outside in the open world, stuttered like crazy as well, so sad. thanks todd.

Saw someone ask how this can possibly be steam deck verified, I’m here to echo that query. 

First and experience: excited for remaster, bought it, refunded in lightspeed. Lack of optimization turns this into Oblivion: The Slideshow even on lowest settings. Shame to call this playable.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the developers removed existing localizations, leaving only an English voiceover.

citations.review_text: These cost-cutting measures by major publishers and their obsession with maximizing profits are just sickening. Not only did they force UE5 onto the Gamebryo engine, which is risky enough on its own, but they also left UE5 as it is and didn’t even bother to optimize it a little. We’ve seen this before from UE5 users. To make the whole thing even more ridiculous, they’ve thrown out the existing localizations and now only offer an English voiceover. Sure, a few things have been expanded here, but with a little good will, they could have taken the old language files and re-recorded the audio where necessary. And the fact that the game is being offered at a price on par with that of the original back then is downright cheeky. AAA titles can now only be bought at a steep discount or in the best-case scenario, not at all anymore.

A very big disappointment so far. I'll probably keep on playing for nostalgia's sake, but all they seem to have focused on is some graphical upgrades. Its the same oblivion you can play in the original and feel the true nostalgia! The only upgrade I hope to experience is the new levelling system, other than that it all feels cheaper and crappier. claims.claim: Reviewers experience heavy stuttering, frame rate drops, and poor overall optimization.

citations.review_text:
Why do I have to download a mod to make this game playable?

I don't often write reviews, but the performance issues with this game made me want to come leave a review, it is that bad. 

I have what most would consider a high end system, yet this game in its vanilla state is practically unplayable. The stuttering, constanst crashes, and ridiculous latency with FSR and frame gen is insane. This has been out for over a year, and still no fix on the horizon. Paying $70 for a game and then having to get a mod to make it somewhat playable is insane work Bethesda.

To be clear, it is absolutely visually stunning, but that is no excuse for a game made by a multi-billion dollar triple-A studio to be basically unplayable, even over a year after release. How THE ♥♥♥♥ is it that some random dude sitting in his basement can publish a mod, fixxing your games performance issues while you the developer, do absolutely nothing about it? IT HAS BEEN OUT FOR OVER A YEAR. THERE HAS BEEN TIME TO FIX THIS. THE GAME NEVER SHOULD HAVE LAUNCHED LIKE THIS.

♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ greedy moronic imbeciles.

Pros: Oblivion

Cons: lackluster melee combat, stiff npcs, alien npc faces (potato faces to knife sharp faces. Too far of an adjustment.), constant graphic glitches, memory leaks requiring restarts, stuttering, load errors, crashes, no bug fixing, poor/nonexistent mod support, cartoonish movement, worse voice actor on the wood elf and others, all at a price tag that is multiples of the original despite it being a glorified reskin.

Classic Bethesda over-hype into a rug-pull. I've played every elder scrolls except the spinoffs and trashline, but I'm skipping VI for at least 6 months, like I did with F4, because of this.

A few years ago (sometime around COVID) I decided to buy the Steam version of the original Oblivion and play through it once more (I finished it back when I was a kid, before Skyrim came out). Honestly, the experience felt like something a certain Skingrad shopkeeper might ask about. But when I got the Remastered version, I felt like a kid again. Both the starter sequence and especially once I was out of the sewers felt fresh and yet deeply familiar, and it was more than worth it to buy the game once more for that feeling alone.
However, the game is unoptimized. My specs below are I would say decent, but running around outside a location (when the game has to load a ton of new stuff) is janky. But once you are in a contained location or not moving from point A to point B, it runs just fine. If that sounds bad, keep in mind that on most new computers the old version literally cannot run without significant modifications (which are not TOO complicated, but are too much for me).

Tried this on my gaming laptop when it first came out...it didn't turn out well. It was completely unoptimized: I put every setting at the lowest it could possibly be, and I couldn't get above 15fps. Just got a new pc, and... I can't even start it. I've done every guide to fix it, but I can't even start it up. I hope Bethesda fixes this game, I was really looking forward to it. May Virtuos never touch another Bethesda IP ever again.

So far I have not had any major issues with the game. I have had stuttering here and there but it last for a few seconds and usually only happens after loading in. The game is just as fun as the original and looks stunning. I also do like the new levelling system.

Its on GamePass with all their other games, just play it there instead of buying it here and wasting your money and supporting this dogwater company. They - neither Bethesda nor Virtuos - haven't updated this game in over a year, since two months after launch, and its still borderline unplayable. Not like it wont run, but like its so freaking annoying that it makes it unbearable and not worth the effort. Theres memory leak issues that cause crashing/stuttering, bugs and glitches and little mod support, which if you've ever played a bethesda game, you know the modding community are the ones that even make their games work right. The longer you play the game the worse it performs, you have to reboot it to fix the stuttering and lagging and 30% FPS drops. I picked this game up basically at launch and to this day I regret it. I've had it for too long, I cant refund it anymore. I waited thinking they would keep updating it and making it better, fixing it like other high profile disaster launches by other companies, but nope. They abandoned it. We got rugpulled based on nostalgia.

Bethesda hasn't announced anything regarding this game, either, with Todd's recent "many words to say little" press releases. Really disappointing. Highly highly do not recommend this, unless its heavily on sale and you're ready for disappointment. I dont know why I expected anything more than this.
Don't waste your money. Unplayable levels of flicker and stutter, and barely runs on the lowest settings with top of the line hardware. what a joke

Cyberpunk ran better than this game on launch and back then I played it on a 6 year old laptop. With newly updated hardware, this game still runs horribly. The intro dungeon had a few stutters, but the second I made it into the overworld, I would be playing at 10 fps. Do not recommend, just play the OG.
As a kid I never had a good enough pc to run this game. Now with adult money and remastered graphics its a replay for the younger self.

In theory, this would be the perfect game to play on the Steamdeck.  In reality however, it's basically unplayable.  Even on the absolute lowest graphics settings, the performance is still pretty bad and there is apparently no intention to optimize the game for PC, let alone the Deck.  

In a sense, it succeeds in its mission of being a remaster in that it has improved graphics and an expanded voice cast and some bug fixes, but what good is all that if it doesn't run well?

I really wanted to love this game, but alas much like any other Bethesda release it runs about as well as Crysis would on a N64. My issue isn't that I have a weak PC, in fact I'm pretty sure this is the only game I've ever played that has this bad stuttering and frame drops. If the game is ever fixed (Bethesda continues support for a full price game challenge impossible) I'd be happy to buy the game again, because the few minutes I did get playing the game at higher that 20 FPS with stutters was quite enjoyable.

TLDR: Unless your rig is in the multiple thousands of dollars in vaule (not counting RAM), then it will not run. I'm refunding this right now.

I'm trying my hardest to fully complete this game, but with the amount of stuttering and shader compilation B.S., It's not looking too good. This is one of the worst performing games I have ever played both visually, and technically. Never out of all my time on PC have I had to download a library full of fixes for a game because the developers refuse to do anything to help it run better and it STILL not being enough.  The funniest part about all this is that apparently it's Steam Deck Verified, which I have no idea how that is even possible in the slightest. If it struggles on decent and even good systems, how in the hell can it POSSIBLY be verified? Maybe with 6x framegen scaling from sub-10fps to get 60fps. Don't even get me started how they somehow managed to raise the file size needed by almost 22x! The original oblivion is not even 6gb and this one is almost 120GB.... unreal (literally). All I'm going to say is that if Bethesda's idea of a remaster is to bloat the file size and remove and change things for the worst and to make sure it's in an absolutely unplayable state even a year after release, I'd tell them to keep TES6, I don't want it.
This game runs so poorly that it's actually baffling. Absolutely zero optimisation whatsoever

It’s a great classic. It looks prettier than the original by far but also has some of that classic jank.
Best story line of all the elder scrolls games. it also has the best guild quests of the series.

But 1 year, no updates.
- Runs very poorly (unoptimised)
- Old bugs haven't been fixed and several NEW bugs have been introduced.

I really cant recommend this performance mess.
And the steam deck verification is a total joke.
This is for me a big betrayal from Bethesta, I got so hyped when this came from nowhere, remake on one of my favorite game of all time, what a huge disappointment...
Very fun game lower fps in certain spots though

[h3]The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered[/h3]

[b]The Short Answer:[/b] 
A nostalgic trip back to Cyrodiil that finally lets you finish what you started years ago, with a heavy melee build that feels great right out of the box—even if VRAM buildup and performance stutters creep in over time.

[b]Recommended For:[/b]
[list]
[*]Returning players looking to hit that classic nostalgia sweet spot and finally cross the finish line on a game they never beat back in the day.
[*]Brawler and warrior builds who love straightforward, satisfying heavy-hitting combat without needing a heavily modded setup.
[/list]

[b]The Good:[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Nostalgic Redemption:[/b] Revisiting Cyrodiil with updated visuals hits like a total time capsule, making it extremely satisfying to finally play through and beat the main campaign properly.
[*][b]Solid Vanilla Combat:[/b] A heavy melee Orc build works smoothly and hits hard without needing third-party mods or complex setup tweaks to feel viable.
[/list]

[b]The Bad:[/b]
[list]
[*][b]VRAM Build-up & Stuttering:[/b] Community reports of memory leaks and performance hitching over extended sessions are very real, especially when moving between the overworld and interior dungeons.
[*][b]Unreal Engine 5 Quirkiness:[/b] Adjusting graphics options mid-session can severely crater frame rates, forcing a full game restart to clear out the lag.
[/list]

[b]Steam Deck Performance:[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Settings/FPS:[/b] Targets a playable 30 FPS on Low settings with TSR or FSR upscaling, though heavy open-world zones will drop frames.
[*][b]Controls & UI:[/b] Full native controller support makes inventory navigation and melee combat feel totally natural on handheld.
[*][b]Battery Life:[/b] ~1.5 to 2 hours max; taxes the handheld APU heavily.
[/list]

[b]Final Score:[/b] 8.5 / 10
Bethesda abandoned the game. No more support means your better off playing the originals. The stuttering is extremely bad, and seemingly gets worse as you progress with your save.

Absolutely amazing game, it's just Oblivion but modernised so you know what you're getting into. As others have said though the performance holds it back massively. I have what I'd consider to be a pretty average PC at this point and I'm well above the supposed "recommended specs", yet it runs terribly if I have Lumen RT on at all. Inside cities and buildings is absolutely fine, but the open world is near unplayable dropping to sub 10fps if an enemy is on screen. You also have horrible hitches and just random FPS drops for no reason. The only way I've been able to play as much as I am is with Lumen RT off, which should be fine, but the game leans on Lumen to light it's world, so without it on the game looks as though they just forgot to bake the lighting, it looks especially bad in forests (which is where most of this game takes place lol). That being said, even with Lumen off it still runs not great, usually a smooth 50 or so fps, but sometimes it still randomly drops for a little bit. 

TL;DR A great remaster of a great game, held back by abysmal performance, forced RT, and abandoned by the devs. I've enjoyed it for sure, but I wouldn't actually recommend it to anyone else unless you have a high tolerance for BS.

This remaster really shows how little Bethesda cares about its customers and its own games. It has been completely abandoned with severe performance issues and bugs across all levels of PC hardware. They talked all about respecting Oblivion with this remaster, then released it completely broken with a new inconsistent and cheap aesthetic.

Cyrodiil is no longer vibrant and colorful. There are maybe 3 different animations the NPCs have while you're talking to them, and they're all cheap and ugly. The sprint animation is just downright ridiculous. Your insanely heavy and powerful armor just contorts all over the place so your character can throw their arms all willy nilly and stick their face in the ground. They gave the game dull, realistic graphics, and made all the character animations in the style of a 3D kids cartoon. The only part of the new animation I like is whacking a dude with my fists and watching their head fly back, but I think that's more a physics thing.

I've tested this game across 5 different computers trying to find the best way to enjoy it. The game is so messed up, it ran at a smooth 30fps at medium settings on a 10 year old computer, while a significantly more powerful modern computer could barely handle anything more, let alone a consistent framerate. Even when you can get it to 60fps at high settings, it will still drop significantly at random when you're outdoors. If you play for too long, performance will tank. If you don't restart the game after changing ONE graphics setting, performance will tank. You can spend hours trying all kinds of combinations of settings (that's actually a huge chunk of my playtime), you can brute force it with raw power, but the game is just broken. Maybe you'll get lucky and have one of the 2 or 3 PC setups (out of the millions possible) the game was optimized for during development. They couldn't even fix the VRAM monitor that only ever shows "0/0". Engine.ini mods did help make the game more bearable, and pr…

I have fully completed the game, nearly all side quests (a couple missing in Shivering Isles), all DLCs, all Daedric quests etc. Even fully finished that cursed Nirnroot quest. Overall the remaster is pretty faithful, other than some slight decorative changes here and there, everything looks very gorgeous and better than the original yet still keeps its insane soul intact. I haven't had a single crash and had pretty decent performance, only slight drops during rain, playing it nearly at all-ultra settings.

I enjoyed the whole game like my first playthrough, though some Oblivion planes, some dungeons (especially the ones in the Shivering Isles) and the whole Shivering Isles content did bore me a bit. I don't know why but the Shivering Isles content did not age well for me. Maybe knowing the story makes it really lame unlike the vanilla quests weirdly.

It sucks that there are so few Steam achievements to match all the content in the game, plus the devs abandoning the game and not fixing obvious performance issues that should not be there is a shame. Still, I do hope to see a Morrowind remaster and have Tamriel Rebuilt by default in it. Let me sink a couple hundred more hours in Morrowind.

I bought the remaster because I was never able to enjoy the original Oblivion, and I always felt bad because I knew there was a great story and experience behind the janky gameplay. While Oblivion: Remastered is, a great game, and I'd say it could've been the definitive way to play Oblivion, I unfortunately cannot recommend this game, the performance is poor, the optimization is hell, more than a year after this game came out it hasn't gotten a single fix, patch, hotfix, nothing, nada. The game doesn't even look impressive, it's just UE5 slop, if you've seen a single "Oblivion: Remaster is an artistic disaster" sort of video, you'd know this is an insult to the original artistic view, and the performance is an insult to whoever has even a slight love for videogames at all.

The gameplay is, of course, great, but that's it, you cannot outweigh everything else with just modern gameplay, as that's what it is, not groundbreaking not revolutionary, just a masterpiece thrown into the slop blender, served, and abandoned.

This is probably one of the more egregious cases of a Triple A studio taking the consumers money and running with it. Post launch support as of me typing this, last update was a little over a year ago and performance issues are still everywhere. Its a shame as I and I presume many others were waiting for performance related patches and there is still nothing. Its safe to say this is abandonware
This game was abandoned with many performance issues and bugs after literally two updates, left at the mercy of players who will fix it with mods anyway. Typical Bethesda move.

My first impressions were great, the game looked nice, it had some lovely soundtracks and I overall enjoyed the gameplay. After like 200 hours into it, without having any bigger issues, my game suddenly began to freeze on the startup screen or it would even crash. It wouldn't load my saves anymore at all. I tried many ways to fix that but nothing helped, so unfortunately I had to leave it. Considering I had barely done any main quests yet, which really bothered me at some point, I got back to it once again. I then came across a video that recommended using certain mods. I would get stuck in certain locations, essential NPCs were stuck or missing, the game wouldn't progress and so on. Only way to avoid that was by reloading older saves and hopefully not having the same issues again, just so annoying. Using console commands could help too but also might break the game even more and it would also disable the achievements (unless using another mod to enable them again). When I finally managed to complete the main story I was so fed up with it and left it for good. As someone that usually prefers to play without mods, I had no other choice here.
